title: Rollback & Hotfix Playbook: severity thresholds, patch-branch rules, and backport workflow
creator: Aisha Banerjee
body:
Purpose:
This ticket captures the canonical playbook for rollbacks and urgent hotfixes across Redwood Inference releases (hosted, dedicated, private). It defines severity criteria, who owns each decision, branch naming and patching guidance, backport rules for LTS and non-LTS channels, verification gates, and communication templates. Goal: reduce time-to-resolution while minimizing customer disruption and preventing cascading regressions.

Summary of key principles:
1) Make low-risk, well-scoped hotfixes via patch branches; prefer backports over full roll-forward when the regression is narrow and reproducible.
2) Rollbacks are allowed only when rollback gate criteria are met (see section "Rollback Gates").
3) All hotfixes must pass an automated smoke & canary validation before broad rollout.
4) LTS branches have stricter backport and test requirements.

Severity classification (decision matrix):
- S0 (Critical): complete service outage or data-loss in production for paying customers, security exploit in the wild. Immediate on-call action; page on-call and Release Lead; expect rollback or hotfix within 30 minutes.
- S1 (High): severe degradation (latency >5x SLO, widespread failures >10% of requests, incorrect model outputs causing major product impact). Page on-call; aim for mitigation or hotfix within 2 hours.
- S2 (Medium): partial degradation, limited customer impact, or UI regressions on non-critical flows. Address in current sprint; schedule hotfix if needed.
- S3 (Low): cosmetic or minor bugs; handle on normal cadence.

Patch branch naming and semantics:
- Naming convention: patch/<component>/<release>-p<patch-number>-<short-desc>
  Example: patch/runtime/runtime-1.22-p1-fix-kv-cache-eviction
- Patch branches are short-lived; merge only via fast-forward into the target branch after PR approval and green checks.
- For backports to multiple channels, create one patch branch per channel (e.g., patch/runtime-1.22-lts-p2 and patch/runtime-1.23-p1).

Backport policy (LTS vs non-LTS):
- LTS channels: Only S0 or S1 issues get automatic consideration for backport. S2/S3 require explicit product approval. Backports must include a minimal test matrix: startup, KV-cache regression repro, canonical inference regression test, and a lightweight integration smoke.
- Non-LTS channels (rolling): More permissive; acceptable for S1/S2 if fix reduces customer pain and risk is low.

Hotfix workflow (step-by-step):
1) Identification: on-call files an incident note and sets severity. Create a hotfix branch following naming rules.
2) Triage & Owner assignment: Release Lead or On-call assigns an engineer and QA lead; notify Product & Customer Success for potential customer impact.
3) Dev & quick test: Implement minimal change, write one deterministic regression test, run unit and component CI locally with the same container image used in production.
4) PR & review: Open PR against the patch branch with link to incident notes and reproduction steps. Must include checklist: changelog entry, rollback plan, risk assessment, test list. Two approvers required: one from Core Runtime and one from Release Engineering.
5) Canary deploy: Deploy to canary pool (1–2% of traffic or single dedicated canary instance depending on surface), run automated canary validation suite (latency profile, token-per-second, KV-cache hits, and correctness tests).
6) Rollout: If canary passes for 30–60 minutes and no new alerts, proceed to staged rollout per rollout policy (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with 10–30 minute holds between stages and automated health checks.
7) Post-deploy verification: Release Lead signs off after end-to-end smoke and dashboard checks. Close incident and file retrospective within 48 hours.

Rollback Gates (when to rollback instead of hotfix):
- Rollback when:
  * Regression introduced by the last deploy is high-severity (S0) and a safe rollback path exists with no data-migration risk, OR
  * Hotfix risk > estimated rollback risk (e.g., hotfix touches multiple services and requires multi-team coordination), OR
  * Canary shows catastrophic failure that cannot be mitigated quickly.
- Do not rollback when:
  * The change involved irreversible DB schema changes or data migrations without a revert path, OR
  * The regression affects a single tenant and an immediate targeted mitigation is possible.

Rollback procedure (executive summary):
1) Confirm last good deploy tag and image hashes across orchestration (k8s manifests) and runtime registries.
2) Quiesce traffic to the bad revision (scale down or reroute) and apply rollback to previous tagged revision.
3) Run smoke tests against the rolled-back revision and monitor health for at least two full alerting windows.
4) Communicate rollback decision to stakeholders (template below).
5) Create hotfix branch off the previous-good commit for a proper fix and backport if necessary.

Testing & Automation requirements:
- Every hotfix PR must trigger the hotfix CI pipeline which includes: unit, integration, canary-simulated load test, and the regression test that reproduces the customer issue.
- Add an automated check that validates branch naming and changelog presence.
- Add to the release bot: when a patch branch is merged, auto-generate release notes entry and trigger automated backport PR creation for configured channels (requires human approval before merging).

Roles & responsibilities:
- Release Lead: decision authority for rollback vs hotfix; coordinates canary and rollout.
- On-call: triage, assignment, first-line mitigation.
- Engineer owner: implements hotfix and ensures tests.
- QA lead: creates and runs smoke/canary validation.
- Customer Success / PM: customer communications and postmortem user impact assessment.

Communication templates (short):
- Interim status (for customers and internal): "We have identified a high-severity regression impacting inference latency for some customers. We are deploying a mitigation and will provide an update within 60 minutes. Incident reference: ENG-5742."
- Rollback announcement: "We are rolling back the most recent deploy (tag: runtime-1.22-20260312) to restore service. Expected downtime: negligible; monitoring is active. A follow-up note will describe root cause and next steps."

Post-incident actions:
- All hotfixes/rollbacks must have a follow-up ticket containing: root cause, full timeline, patch branches created/merged, tests added, and list of customers impacted.
- If the incident was S0/S1, include a retro with action items and a deadline for backports for LTS channels.

Open items / proposed automations:
- Add an automated risk-scoring check that suggests rollback vs hotfix based on change footprint.
- Integrate release bot with Slack to auto-announce patch branch creation and canary passes/fails.

References and artifacts: link to runbooks, release bot commands, and staging dashboards are in the links field below.

Intended next steps:
- 1) Validate playbook with on-call rotation during next sim-week (owner: Marco).
- 2) Implement hotfix CI pipeline changes (owner: ENG-5710).
- 3) Ship naming/automation changes in release-bot (owner: ENG-5601).
